title: 航空システム専門実験・演習B
subtitle: Aeronautics Major Lab/Exercises B
keywords: Planning of tests 2.Performance evaluation 3.Summarizing data 4.Oral presentation 5.Aeronautical engineering
educationalGoal: Students will: (1)learn the method and theory of a selected basic subject through an experiment and practice. (2)acquire deeper understandings and ability to apply them for various engineering subjects. (3)learn how to write the experimental method in an experiment report. (4)learn how to prepare and make a presentation on the experiments and results.
advice: Students will carry out the following experiments in Exercise B. Details of the experiments can be confirmed in the textbook. ①Wind tunnel test ②Jet engine performance test ③Flight dynamics Students attending the lecture will be divided into three groups(A,B,C). Group A will carry out the experiment ① for five weeks and then the experiment ② for the next five weeks and finally the experiment ③ for another five weeks. Group B will follow the order of ②→③→①, and group C will follow the order of ③→①→②. In addition, the class details are distributed at the time of the start of each experimental theme.
books: Textbooks: Aeronautics Major Experiments and Exercises B Reference books:None Reserved books:Introduction of Aircraft Design (in Japanese), Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun, Ltd., Introduction of Aircraft Design 2 (in Japanese), Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun, Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: Students should read the textbook before an experiment and understand what kind of experiment they will be carrying out. In addition, students should make a report properly before a class as preparation, if any for that class.

Be able to carry out experiments safely base on understandings of the principle of an experiment and the measure
Be able to analyze experimental data using computers and to explain the key points and problems appropriately.
Be able to interpret an experimental phenomenon based on learned technical knowledge and to evaluate the validit
Be able to explain the obtained test data reasonably by comparing them with analytical solutions precisely.

achievementLevels.ideal: ① i) Explain the cylinder pressure distribution from the flow. ii) Explain the drag errors caused by measurement methods. iii) Explain precisely the forces and moment acting on the wing, and the difference between theory and experiment. ② Students properly explain engine operational principal, basic structures, operational characteristics and engine performance relating to the main components of the turbojet engine. ③Students properly explain the generation of wing lift, the principle of flight stability, properly record experimental data, and properly explain difference from experimental model and actual aircraft with them.
achievementLevels.standard: ① i) Explain the cylinder pressure distribution. ii) Explain the cylinder drag. iii) Explain the forces and moment acting on the wing. ②Students can understand engine operational principal and record properly performance test data. Students also can understand and explain the trend of engine performance based on the operational characteristics ③Students roughly explain the generation of wing lift, the principle of flight stability, roughly record experimental data, and roughly explain difference from experimental model and actual aircraft with them.

lessons.content: [Students understand learning objectives, outline and target abilities of this course based on distributed syllabus. Especially, students understand which part this course assumes within learning objectives of department of aeronautics and rough concrete level of achievement.] ① Wind tunnel test Explanation of experimental equipment and measuring device. Confirmation of prior knowledge. Verification of wind velocity. Measurement of pressure distribution on cylinder surface. Estimation of cylinder drag. Flow visualization around cylinder.
lessons.assignments: [Students understand the relation between learning objectives of department of aeronautics and this course.] ①Prepare for the pressure distributions on cylinder surface. Prepare for the numerical integration.

lessons.content: Measurements of wake velocity of cylinder Estimation of cylinder drag by momentum method Direct measurements of cylinder drag
Joukowsky transform Calculation of wind velocity and pressure distribution of Joukowsky airfoil Estimation of the lift acting on airfoil
Measurements of forces and moment acting on airfoil Drawing lift and drag and moment curves Drawing polar curve
lessons.assignments: Prepare for lift and drag acting on the wing

lessons.content: Presentation and discussion Students self-check the content of the experiments, reports, presentation and attendance.
lessons.assignments: Prepare the presentation by studying literatures for question and answer.

lessons.content: ②Jet engine performance test Students will learn the basic structure of the aero engine, operational principal and performance measurement system. Observation of the engine basic structure using a cut model of turbojet engine and measurement of major dimensions of the engine. Observation and review of the engine performance test facility, measurement items and devises, measurement methods.
lessons.operation: Lecture and meeting Confirmation of an experiment practice work procedure and work allocation in the experiments.
lessons.assignments: Preparation of the test by reading the textbook. Review of the gas turbine cycle such as T-S diagram and p-v diagram.

lessons.content: Engine performance test Analyze the obtained test data
lessons.assignments: Review of proceeding lessons and prepare for an engine performance test.

lessons.content: Analyses of the obtained test data Evaluation of the engine performance of tested turbojet engine
lessons.assignments: Review and check of the analytical results Analyses of the obtained test data

lessons.content: Presentation and discussion on the test results and engine performance analyses Modification of the analyses based on the specified points in the presentation Preparation of a final report
lessons.assignments: Prepare the test report Prepare the presentation by surveying literatures for a question and answer session

lessons.content: Perform self-check for the contents of the experiments, reports and oral presentation
lessons.assignments: Self-check the contents of the lecture, experiment and theory

lessons.content: ③Flight dynamics Equipment : Flight demonstration wind tunnel Flight dynamics test(1) : aerodynamic properties Investigation for the lift characteristics of the aircraft model as the angle of attack is varied. Comparison between experimental data and the theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.

Flight dynamics test(2) : trim and neutral point Investigation for static stability and neutral point of the aircraft model as the the center of gravity is moved. Comparison between experimental data and the theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook from p.B-3-6 to p.B-3-25 Create 2nd report

lessons.content: Flight dynamics test(3) : short period oscillation and phugoid oscillation Investigation for dynamic stability of the aircraft model as free flight is carried. Comparison between experimental data and the theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook from p.B-3-26 to p.B-3-31 Create 3rd report

lessons.content: Flight dynamics test(4) : stall Investigation for stall characteristics of the aircraft model by flow visualization. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook from p.B-3-32 top.B-3-36 Create 4th report

lessons.content: Oral presentation and integrated learning Review and self-evaluation.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for oral presentation Self-evaluation on achievement in this course
